from __future__ import annotations

import re
from collections import Counter

_WORD_RE = re.compile(r"[a-z']+", re.IGNORECASE)


def top_words(text: str, k: int) -> list[tuple[str, int]]:
    """Return the ``k`` most common words in ``text`` as ``(word, count)`` tuples.

    A word is a maximal run of ASCII letters and apostrophes (so ``"don't"`` is one word and
    ``"well-known"`` is two), compared case-insensitively and reported in lower case.
    Results are sorted by count descending, then alphabetically.
    """
    if k <= 0:
        return []
    counts = Counter(word.lower() for word in _WORD_RE.findall(text) if any(c != "'" for c in word))
    return sorted(counts.items(), key=lambda item: (-item[1], item[0]))[:k]
